amoled.blurb: adds an AMOLED target, with a sparse always-on sleep frame
amoled.text:
# A face that also targets an AMOLED watch, with an always-on sleep frame.
#
# An AMOLED screen that stayed on all day would burn in, so while the watch
# sleeps it draws a separate, sparse frame instead (docs/guide/always-on-display.md).
# You don't write a second design: `aod:` on an element is a block of
# overrides for that frame (writing one also shows it; `visible: false`
# hides it), and `defaults: {aod: ...}` below is the same block for every
# element that says nothing.
#
# Here everything is hidden asleep except the clock, drawn as a thin outline
# around black digits, and a dimmer, thinner battery ring. `dim:` scales every
# colour the sleep frame draws; the clock's own `dim: 1` keeps its outline
# at full brightness. A moving pixel mask is on by default, so no pixel
# stays lit two minutes running.
#
# The MIP watches in `targets:` are always on already and ignore `aod:`.
#
# Preview the sleep frame with:  wfb preview <file> -d fenix847mm --aod
#
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vvorth/garmin-wf-builder/main/schema/wfb-face-2.schema.json

format: 2

face:
  id: __UUID__
  name: __NAME__
  version: 1.0.0

build:
  targets: [fenix847mm, fenix8solar47mm, fenix8solar51mm, fr955]
defaults:
  aod:
    visible: false
    dim: 0.6

resources:
  palette:
    black: "#000000"
    white: "#FFFFFF"
    gray: "#AAAAAA"
    dark: "#555555"
    accent: "#00AAFF"
    hot: "#FF5500"

elements:
  background:
    type: rectangle
    at: { anchor: center }
    size: { width: 100%, height: 100% }
    color: color.black

  date:
    type: text
    text: "{date.today:%a %d %b}"
    font: FONT_TINY
    at: { anchor: center, dy: -36%r }
    color: color.gray

  clock:
    type: text
    text: "{time.clock:%h:%M}"
    font: FONT_NUMBER_HOT
    at: { anchor: center }
    color: color.white
    aod:
      dim: 1
      color: color.black   # hollow digits: only the outline lights
      outline:
        width: 2
        color: color.gray

  heart:
    type: group
    size: { width: 30%r, height: 12%r }
    at: { anchor: center, dy: 38%r }
    on_hold: heart_rate
    children:
      hr_icon:
        type: icon
        icon: heart
        size: 10%r
        at: { anchor: left }
        align: left
        color: color.hot
      hr_value:
        type: text
        text: "{heart_rate.current:d}"
        font: FONT_TINY
        at: { anchor: left, dx: 13%r }
        align: left
        color: color.white
        absent: "--"

  battery_ring:
    type: gauge
    style: arc
    value: system.battery
    max: 100
    at: { anchor: center }
    radius: 90%r
    thickness: 3%r
    start_angle: 210deg
    sweep: 300deg
    color: color.accent
    track_color: color.dark
    aod:
      thickness: 1%r
      color: color.dark

analog.blurb: a three-hand dial with ticks, numerals and a date window
analog.text:
# A classic three-hand dial: minute and hour ticks, twelve numerals, a date
# window at 3 o'clock, and hour, minute and second hands.
#
# The dial -- ticks, numerals, the window's frame -- never changes, so it sits
# in `static:` and is painted once into a buffer rather than every second.
#
# A hand is drawn pointing at 12 o'clock in a frame whose origin is its axis
# (docs/guide/analog-hands.md); the watch turns it. `dy` is negative towards
# the tip. The second hand vanishes while the watch sleeps (`seconds: awake`,
# the default) -- a MIP face redraws only once a minute then.
#
# Preview a flattering time with:  wfb preview <file> --time 10:09:42
#
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vvorth/garmin-wf-builder/main/schema/wfb-face-2.schema.json

format: 2

face:
  id: __UUID__
  name: __NAME__
  version: 1.0.0

build:
  targets: [fenix8solar47mm, fenix8solar51mm, fr955]
resources:
  palette:
    bg: "#000000"
    fg: "#FFFFFF"
    dim: "#AAAAAA"
    accent: "#FF5500"

  hand_sets:
    classic:
      hour:
        color: color.fg
        parts:
          - type: polygon
            points:
              - { dx: -3%r, dy: 8%r } # a short tail behind the axis
              - { dx: -2%r, dy: -40%r }
              - { dy: -46%r } # the tip
              - { dx: 2%r, dy: -40%r }
              - { dx: 3%r, dy: 8%r }
      minute:
        color: color.fg
        parts:
          - { type: rectangle, at: { dy: -32%r }, size: { width: 3%r, height: 76%r } }
      second:
        color: color.accent
        parts:
          - { type: line, at: { dy: 15%r }, to: { dy: -84%r }, thickness: 2px }
          - { type: circle, at: { dy: 15%r }, radius: 3%r }  # counterweight

static:
  background:
    type: rectangle
    at: { anchor: center }
    size: { width: 100%, height: 100% }
    color: color.bg

  minute_ticks:
    type: pattern
    pattern: radial
    at: { anchor: center } # the point every copy turns about
    count: 60 # step defaults to 360deg / 60 = 6deg
    skip_every: 5 # leave the hour positions to hour_ticks
    color: color.dim
    parts: # copy 0, as it looks at 12 o'clock
      - { type: line, at: { dy: -96%r }, to: { dy: -90%r }, thickness: 1px }

  hour_ticks:
    type: pattern
    pattern: radial
    at: { anchor: center }
    count: 12
    color: color.fg
    parts:
      - { type: rectangle, at: { dy: -90%r }, size: { width: 3%r, height: 10%r } }

  # One radial pattern instead of twelve text elements. `copy` is the copy's
  # index, 0 at 12 o'clock, so this draws 12, 1, 2, ... 11. The 3 is skipped:
  # the date window sits there.
  numerals:
    type: pattern
    pattern: radial
    at: { anchor: center }
    count: 12
    skip: [3]
    color: color.dim
    parts:
      - type: text
        text: "{(copy + 11) % 12 + 1}"
        font: FONT_SMALL
        at: { dy: -70%r }

  date_frame:
    type: rectangle
    filled: false
    thickness: 1px
    at: { anchor: center, dx: 62%r }
    size: { width: 26%r, height: 18%r }
    color: color.dim

elements:
  date:
    type: text
    text: "{date.day:d}"
    font: FONT_TINY
    at: { anchor: center, dx: 62%r }
    color: color.fg

  hands:
    type: hands
    set: classic
    at: { anchor: center }
  pin:
    type: circle
    at: { anchor: center }
    radius: 3%r
    color: color.accent

calendar.blurb: the time over a Monday-first month of dots, today lit
calendar.text:
# The time over a month at a glance: a Monday-first calendar of dots, today
# lit and the days already gone dimmed, under a row of weekday initials.
#
# Both are `pattern: grid` -- one template repeated in rows of `columns:`.
# Inside a pattern, `copy` is the index of the copy being drawn (0, 1, 2 ...),
# so a colour, a text part or a part's `visible:` can differ per copy
# (docs/guide/patterns.md "Grids").
#
# The grid has 37 cells -- enough for a 31-day month starting on a Sunday.
# `first` below is the column the 1st falls in, worked out from today's
# weekday and date (`date.weekday` is 1 for Sunday, so `+ 5` makes Monday
# column 0; the `+ 35` keeps the `%` operand positive). The cells before it
# are hidden. A pattern cannot know the month's length, so a short month
# still draws 31 dots: the last ones simply never light.
#
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vvorth/garmin-wf-builder/main/schema/wfb-face-2.schema.json

format: 2

face:
  id: __UUID__
  name: __NAME__
  version: 1.0.0

build:
  targets: [fenix8solar47mm, fenix8solar51mm, fr955]
resources:
  palette:
    bg: "#000000"
    fg: "#FFFFFF"
    past: "#AAAAAA"
    today: "#FFAA00"

static:
  background:
    type: rectangle
    at: { anchor: center }
    size: { width: 100%, height: 100% }
    color: color.bg

  # Reads only `copy`, so it never changes and can live in `static:`.
  weekdays:
    type: pattern
    pattern: grid
    at: { anchor: center, dx: -42%r, dy: -14%r } # copy 0's place
    count: 7
    columns: 7
    step: { dx: 14%r }
    color: color.past
    parts:
      - type: text
        text: >-
          {(copy == 0 ? "M" : copy == 1 ? "T" : copy == 2 ? "W" : copy == 3 ? "T" :
          copy == 4 ? "F" : copy == 5 ? "S" : "S")}
        font: FONT_XTINY

elements:
  clock:
    type: text
    text: "{time.clock:%h:%M}"
    font: FONT_NUMBER_MEDIUM
    at: { anchor: center, dy: -54%r }
    color: color.fg

  month:
    type: text
    text: "{date.today:%b %Y}"
    font: FONT_XTINY
    at: { anchor: center, dy: -30%r }
    color: color.today

  # first = (date.weekday + 5 - (date.day - 1) + 35) % 7, written out inline:
  # a pattern expression cannot name an intermediate value.
  days:
    type: pattern
    pattern: grid
    at: { anchor: center, dx: -42%r, dy: -2%r }
    count: 37
    columns: 7
    step: { dx: 14%r, dy: 11%r }
    color: >-
      copy == (date.weekday + 41 - date.day) % 7 + date.day - 1 ? color.today : (copy < (date.weekday + 41 - date.day) % 7 + date.day - 1 ? color.past : color.fg)
    parts:
      - type: circle
        radius: 3%r
        visible: "copy >= (date.weekday + 41 - date.day) % 7 && copy < (date.weekday + 41 - date.day) % 7 + 31"

dashboard.blurb: time, a goal ring, two data clusters and a battery bar
dashboard.text:
# A denser starting point: the time, a goal ring, two data clusters and battery.
#
# Offsets are in %r -- percentages of the screen's minor radius -- so the design
# keeps its proportions on both the 260x260 and 280x280 families rather than
# drifting. Use %r for anything you think of as "this far out from the middle".
#
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vvorth/garmin-wf-builder/main/schema/wfb-face-2.schema.json

format: 2

face:
  id: __UUID__
  name: __NAME__
  version: 1.0.0

build:
  targets: [fenix8solar47mm, fenix8solar51mm, fr955]
resources:
  palette:
    bg: "#000000"
    text: "#FFFFFF"
    dim: "#AAAAAA"
    accent: "#00AAFF"
    hot: "#FF5500"
    track: "#555555"

static:
  background:
    type: rectangle
    at: { anchor: center }
    size: { width: 100%, height: 100% }
    color: color.bg

elements:
  # A stroked ring, open at the bottom. There is no filled-sector primitive in
  # Connect IQ, so `thickness` is a pen width and there is no inner radius.
  step_ring:
    type: gauge
    style: arc
    value: activity.steps
    max: activity.step_goal
    at: { anchor: center }
    radius: 88%r
    thickness: 9px
    start_angle: 215deg # measured clockwise from 12 o'clock
    sweep: 290deg
    color: color.accent
    track_color: color.track
    absent: hide      # required: both bindings can be absent

  clock:
    type: text
    text: "{time.clock:%h:%M}"
    font: FONT_NUMBER_HOT
    at: { anchor: center, dy: -12%r }
    color: color.text

  hr_icon:
    type: icon
    icon: heart
    size: 11%r
    at: { anchor: center, dx: -40%r, dy: 30%r }
    color: color.hot

  hr_value:
    type: text
    text: "{heart_rate.current:d}"
    font: FONT_TINY
    at: { anchor: center, dx: -17%r, dy: 30%r }
    color: color.text
    absent: "--"

  steps_icon:
    type: icon
    icon: steps
    size: 11%r
    at: { anchor: center, dx: 13%r, dy: 30%r }
    color: color.accent

  steps_value:
    type: text
    text: "{activity.steps / 1000:.01f}"
    font: FONT_TINY
    at: { anchor: center, dx: 38%r, dy: 30%r }
    color: color.text
    absent: "--"

  battery:
    type: gauge
    style: bar
    value: system.battery
    max: 100
    at: { anchor: center, dy: 62%r }
    size: { width: 40%r, height: 5%r }
    color: color.text
    track_color: color.track

gauge.blurb: a battery needle gauge over the top half, the time below it
gauge.text:
# An instrument-style face: a battery gauge across the top half, its needle
# turning from E at 9 o'clock to F at 3, and the time below the axis, where
# the needle never goes.
#
# A needle (`gauge` with `style: needle`) is authored like an analog
# hand -- its parts point at 12 o'clock, in a frame whose origin is the axis
# -- and turns to `start_angle + value / max x sweep`, clockwise from 12
# (docs/guide/progress-and-graphs.md "Gauge needles"). The tick ring is a
# radial `pattern` sharing the needle's start angle and sweep: 11 ticks
# 18 degrees apart span the same 180 degrees.
#
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vvorth/garmin-wf-builder/main/schema/wfb-face-2.schema.json

format: 2

face:
  id: __UUID__
  name: __NAME__
  version: 1.0.0

build:
  targets: [fenix8solar47mm, fenix8solar51mm, fr955]
resources:
  palette:
    bg: "#000000"
    fg: "#FFFFFF"
    scale: "#AAAAAA"
    accent: "#FFAA00"
    low: "#FF0000"

static:
  background:
    type: rectangle
    at: { anchor: center }
    size: { width: 100%, height: 100% }
    color: color.bg

  battery_ticks:
    type: pattern
    pattern: radial
    at: { anchor: center }
    count: 11
    start: 270deg
    step: 18deg
    color: color.scale
    parts:
      - { type: line, at: { dy: -94%r }, to: { dy: -84%r }, thickness: 2px }

  empty_mark:
    type: text
    text: "E"
    font: FONT_XTINY
    at: { anchor: center, dx: -76%r, dy: 12%r }
    color: color.low

  full_mark:
    type: text
    text: "F"
    font: FONT_XTINY
    at: { anchor: center, dx: 76%r, dy: 12%r }
    color: color.scale

elements:
  # A colour may read data: the needle turns red below 20%. Parts without a
  # colour of their own take the element's.
  battery_needle:
    type: gauge
    style: needle
    value: system.battery
    max: 100
    at: { anchor: center }
    start_angle: 270deg
    sweep: 180deg
    color: "system.battery < 20 ? color.low : color.accent"
    needle:
      - type: polygon
        points: [{ dx: -3%r, dy: 10%r }, { dx: -1%r, dy: -74%r },  dy: -80%r, { dx: 1%r, dy: -74%r }, { dx: 3%r, dy: 10%r }]
      - { type: circle, radius: 6%r, color: color.fg }    # the hub, drawn last

  clock:
    type: text
    text: "{time.clock:%h:%M}"
    font: FONT_NUMBER_MEDIUM
    at: { anchor: center, dy: 38%r }
    color: color.fg

  date:
    type: text
    text: "{date.today:%a %d}"
    font: FONT_XTINY
    at: { anchor: center, dy: 64%r }
    color: color.scale

minimal.blurb: a background and the time -- the smallest face worth building
minimal.text:
# The smallest face worth building: a background and the time.
#
# Everything here uses a system font, so this design needs no asset files at all.
# To use your own typeface, add a `fonts:` block and point an element at it:
#
#   fonts:
#     clock:
#       source: assets/YourFont.ttf
#       size: 18%r          # of this device's minor radius (px and %r only)
#
#   ...then `font: font.clock` on the text element.
#
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vvorth/garmin-wf-builder/main/schema/wfb-face-2.schema.json

format: 2

face:
  id: __UUID__
  name: __NAME__
  version: 1.0.0

build:
  targets: [fenix8solar47mm, fenix8solar51mm, fr955]

# Every channel is 0x00, 0x55, 0xAA or 0xFF -- the only values a 64-colour MIP
# panel shows without dithering. The linter checks this.
resources:
  palette:
    bg: "#000000"
    text: "#FFFFFF"
    dim: "#AAAAAA"

static:
  background:
    type: rectangle
    at: { anchor: center }
    size: { width: 100%, height: 100% }
    color: color.bg

elements:
  clock:
    type: text
    text: "{time.clock:%h:%M}"
    # %h follows the watch's own 12/24-hour setting, which %H and %I do not.
    font: FONT_NUMBER_HOT
    at: { anchor: center }
    color: color.text

  seconds:
    type: text
    text: "{time.second:02d}"
    font: FONT_SMALL
    at: { anchor: center, dy: 30%r }
    color: color.dim

navy_classic.blurb: a navy sunray dress dial: polygon hands, batons, a day/date window at 3

palette.blurb: all 64 MIP colours as named swatches, with a colour scheme and colour axes

sport.blurb: time, a heart-rate graph and four readouts, distance in the wearer's units
sport.text:
# A data-heavy digital face: the time, a heart-rate graph, and four
# icon-and-value readouts, with a battery bar at the bottom.
#
# Each readout is a `group`: a box of its own that its children are placed
# inside, so moving the group moves both. Holding a group opens the matching
# Garmin glance (`on_hold:`) -- the one gesture a live face gets.
#
# `activity.distance` arrives in centimetres; `units: auto` shows it in km or
# miles, whichever the wearer chose on the watch, and `{unit}` prints the
# label. Try `wfb preview <file> --units statute`.
#
# Every reading here can be absent (no heart-rate lock yet, a fresh day), so
# each says what to draw instead: `absent: "--"`.
#
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vvorth/garmin-wf-builder/main/schema/wfb-face-2.schema.json

format: 2

face:
  id: __UUID__
  name: __NAME__
  version: 1.0.0

build:
  targets: [fenix8solar47mm, fenix8solar51mm, fr955]
resources:
  palette:
    bg: "#000000"
    fg: "#FFFFFF"
    dim: "#AAAAAA"
    track: "#555555"
    hot: "#FF5500"
    accent: "#00AAFF"
    good: "#00FF00"
    low: "#FF0000"

static:
  background:
    type: rectangle
    at: { anchor: center }
    size: { width: 100%, height: 100% }
    color: color.bg

elements:
  date:
    type: text
    text: "{date.today:%a %d %b}"
    font: FONT_XTINY
    at: { anchor: center, dy: -66%r }
    color: color.dim

  clock:
    type: text
    text: "{time.clock:%h:%M}"
    font: FONT_NUMBER_MEDIUM
    at: { anchor: center, dy: -38%r }
    color: color.fg

  # The last four hours of heart rate, time-binned on the watch. `wfb series`
  # lists the other series a face may plot.
  hr_graph:
    type: graph
    series: heart_rate
    range: 4h
    style: area
    at: { anchor: center, dy: -2%r }
    size: { width: 70%r, height: 22%r }
    min: auto
    max: auto
    color: color.hot
    on_hold: heart_rate

  hr:
    type: group
    size: { width: 42%r, height: 12%r }
    at: { anchor: center, dx: -50%r, dy: 22%r }
    align: left
    on_hold: heart_rate
    children:
      hr_icon:
        type: icon
        icon: heart
        size: 9%r
        at: { anchor: left }
        align: left
        color: color.hot
      hr_value:
        type: text
        text: "{heart_rate.current:d}"
        font: FONT_XTINY
        at: { anchor: left, dx: 12%r }
        align: left
        color: color.fg
        absent: "--"

  steps:
    type: group
    size: { width: 42%r, height: 12%r }
    at: { anchor: center, dx: 8%r, dy: 22%r }
    align: left
    on_hold: steps
    children:
      steps_icon:
        type: icon
        icon: steps
        size: 9%r
        at: { anchor: left }
        align: left
        color: color.accent
      steps_value:
        type: text
        text: "{activity.steps / 1000.0:.1f}k"
        font: FONT_XTINY
        at: { anchor: left, dx: 12%r }
        align: left
        color: color.fg
        absent: "--"

  distance:
    type: group
    size: { width: 42%r, height: 12%r }
    at: { anchor: center, dx: -50%r, dy: 42%r }
    align: left
    children:
      distance_icon:
        type: icon
        icon: distance
        size: 9%r
        at: { anchor: left }
        align: left
        color: color.good
      distance_value:
        type: text
        text: "{activity.distance:.1f}{unit}"
        units: auto
        font: FONT_XTINY
        at: { anchor: left, dx: 12%r }
        align: left
        color: color.fg
        absent: "--"

  calories:
    type: group
    size: { width: 42%r, height: 12%r }
    at: { anchor: center, dx: 8%r, dy: 42%r }
    align: left
    on_hold: calories
    children:
      calories_icon:
        type: icon
        icon: flame
        size: 9%r
        at: { anchor: left }
        align: left
        color: color.hot
      calories_value:
        type: text
        text: "{activity.calories:d}"
        font: FONT_XTINY
        at: { anchor: left, dx: 12%r }
        align: left
        color: color.fg
        absent: "--"

  # A colour may read data: the bar turns red below 20%.
  battery:
    type: gauge
    style: bar
    value: system.battery
    max: 100
    at: { anchor: center, dy: 64%r }
    size: { width: 36%r, height: 5%r }
    color: "system.battery < 20 ? color.low : color.good"
    track_color: color.track
    on_hold: battery

themed.blurb: light/dark schemes, accent colours and two complication slots set on the watch
themed.text:
# A face the wearer restyles on the watch itself: a light or dark scheme, an
# accent colour, a data colour, and two complication slots whose content they
# pick -- all from the fēnix 8's own watch face editor, with no phone app.
#
# The editor has exactly four axes (docs/guide/configuration.md):
#
# * `style:` -- each entry names a `scheme:` from `theme:`, a set of roles
#   (`color.bg`, `.fg`, ...) that switch together;
# * `accent_color:` and `data_color:` -- one colour each, `color.accent`
#   and `color.data`;
# * `slots:` -- named complication slots, drawn by `type: data`.
#
# A watch without the editor (the Forerunner 955 is one) offers the same
# choices in a settings menu the build generates; one with neither keeps
# every `default:` forever, and the linter says so.
#
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://raw.githubusercontent.com/vvorth/garmin-wf-builder/main/schema/wfb-face-2.schema.json

format: 2

face:
  id: __UUID__
  name: __NAME__
  version: 1.0.0

build:
  targets: [fenix8solar47mm, fenix8solar51mm, fr955]

# Every channel is 0x00, 0x55, 0xAA or 0xFF, the colours a MIP panel shows
# without dithering -- including every choice offered below.
resources:
  palette:
    black: "#000000"
    white: "#FFFFFF"
    light_gray: "#AAAAAA"
    dark_gray: "#555555"
    orange: "#FF5500"
    amber: "#FFAA00"
    cyan: "#00FFFF"
    sky_blue: "#00AAFF"
    lime: "#AAFF00"

theme:
  schemes:
    dark:
      label: "Dark"
      colors: { bg: color.black, fg: color.white, dim: color.light_gray }
    light:
      label: "Light"
      colors: { bg: color.white, fg: color.black, dim: color.dark_gray }

config:
  style:
    default: dark
    choices:
      dark: { scheme: dark }
      light: { scheme: light }
  accent_color:
    default: color.orange
    choices: [color.orange, color.amber, color.cyan, color.lime]
  data_color:
    default: color.sky_blue
    choices: [color.sky_blue, color.white, color.amber]
  slots:
    top:
      default: body_battery
      choices: any # the editor's own full complication picker
    bottom:
      default: steps
      choices: [steps, heart_rate, calories]

static:
  # A config colour in `static:` is repainted when the wearer changes it.
  background:
    type: rectangle
    at: { anchor: center }
    size: { width: 100%, height: 100% }
    color: color.bg
    # One allow anywhere accepts the single, face-wide warning.

  accent_ring:
    type: arc
    at: { anchor: center }
    radius: 94%r
    thickness: 4px
    start_angle: 0deg
    sweep: 360deg
    color: color.accent

elements:
  date:
    type: text
    text: "{date.today:%a %d}"
    font: FONT_TINY
    at: { anchor: center, dy: -40%r }
    color: color.dim

  clock:
    type: text
    text: "{time.clock:%h:%M}"
    font: FONT_NUMBER_HOT
    at: { anchor: center, dy: 6%r }
    color: color.fg

  # A slot draws the chosen complication's icon and reading. It takes no
  # format spec -- the reading's type depends on what the wearer picks.
  top_slot:
    type: data
    slot: top
    at: { anchor: center, dy: -66%r }
    font: FONT_SMALL
    icon: { size: 14%r, gap: 2%r, color: color.accent }
    color: color.data
    short: true # 7-character weather and training-status names
    absent: "--"
    on_hold: auto # opens the glance for whatever the slot shows

  bottom_slot:
    type: data
    slot: bottom
    at: { anchor: center, dy: 52%r }
    font: FONT_SMALL
    icon: { size: 14%r, gap: 2%r, color: color.accent }
    color: color.data
    absent: "--"
    on_hold: auto
